ai.title: Project understanding agent replaces workspace profiler on GPT-6 Luna
ai.summary: The workspace profiler subsystem is renamed to project understanding, with the agent ID changed from `freebuff-workspace-profiler` to `freebuff-project-understanding` and its model switched from DeepSeek V4 Flash to GPT-6 Luna to prevent project files from reaching DeepSeek's API. The agent is built at runtime from a backend-served template, runs four reading rounds before forcing a `set_output` call, and offers only `list_directory`, `glob`, `read_files`, and `set_output` tools. The SDK gains two new `RunOptions` flags: `confineFileToolsToProject` (backs a new `ProjectFence` that refuses paths outside `cwd` via symlink-resolved containment) and `refuseNonTextFileReads` (refuses non-text extensions and NUL-siffed binaries via a shared `non-text-files` module). This is one of five distinct changes; others include a new `DESKTOP_PROJECT_UNDERSTANDING` analytics event, a `broad-roots` guard that blocks home/Desktop/Documents/system paths, and a cost-estimation helper pinned to GPT-6 Luna's OpenRouter standard-tier list prices.

changes.what: Renamed the workspace-profile module to project-understanding, switched the agent model to GPT-6 Luna, and tightened its tool set to four read-only tools.

Added the SDK-side project-understanding client, a due-check/report API against `/api/v1/project-understanding`, and a `countProjectFiles` helper that respects read limits and the non-text guard.

Added `confineFileToolsToProject` and `refuseNonTextFileReads` to `RunOptions`, a new `ProjectFence` that rejects paths outside `cwd` as written or through symlinks, and per-tool enforcement in `handleToolCall` for `code_search`, `list_directory`, `glob`, and `read_files`.

ai.title: Add lean context budget prompt to base3 agent for 100k models
ai.summary: A new `lean` flag on `RootCompactionPolicy` (defined in `common/src/constants/compaction-policy.ts` with `maxContextLength` of 110k) triggers a context-budget section in the base3 agent's system prompt. The section, generated by `leanContextGuidance` in the new `agents/lean-context.ts`, instructs the model to read narrowly and keep every request under 100k prompt tokens. This allows eval pairs (added in `agents/base3-haiku-5-5-lean-evals.ts`) to isolate the performance impact of the budget on Claude Haiku 5.5, which OpenRouter prices at a premium above 100k tokens. Supporting changes add `ContextLogEntry` tracking in the buffbench runners and a new model picker placement for the 100k-context row.
ai.evidence: New file `agents/lean-context.ts` exports `leanContextGuidance`, which `agents/base3.ts` now imports and appends to the system prompt when the `lean` flag and `maxContextLength` are set on the compaction policy. `common/src/constants/compaction-policy.ts` adds `RootCompactionPolicy` and `LEAN_COMPACTION_POLICY` with `maxContextLength: 110_000`. New eval files `agents/base3-haiku-5-5-evals.ts` and `agents/base3-haiku-5-5-lean-evals.ts` pair a full-context run with a lean-budget run of Claude Haiku 5.5 in buffbench, and `evals/buffbench/runners/runner.ts` introduces `ContextLogEntry` to capture per-request usage and compaction events.

testNames: scales what was added since the receipt by the receipt's input ratio
clamps an implausible ratio, and an older anchor without one adds 1:1

facts: Provider input tokens per estimated token in that request. Content added since is scaled by it; absent on older anchors (scale 1).

Latest receipt plus the estimated change since it. String lengths, not tokenization, keep startup/resume/missing-usage paths cheap even for long runs of repeated characters. A model switch invalidates the anchor.

The change is scaled by the anchor's own provider-to-estimate ratio, so a model whose tokenizer reads code at 1.4x the estimate is not under-counted by 40% of everything added since the last request. That error was the margin a compaction threshold had to leave below a hard limit.
Input only: output tokens can include reasoning the next prompt never carries, which would read as a denser tokenizer than the model has.
The anchor's calibration (`contextTokenBaseline.scale`), so this edit is counted as estimateContextTokens would count it.
A legacy/external rewrite can remove more estimated tokens than the provider ever counted. Fall back rather than calling that empty context.

ai.title: Context token estimation adds per-model calibration scale
ai.summary: The agent runtime now calibrates context token estimates against the provider's actual token count to fix systematic under-counting for models with dense tokenizers. `recordContextUsage` computes a `scale` factor as the ratio of provider input tokens to estimated input tokens, clamped between `MIN_SCALE` (0.5) and `MAX_SCALE` (2.5). `estimateContextTokens` and `adjustContextTokenCountForHistoryEdit` multiply subsequent token deltas by this scale so that added content reflects the model's real tokenizer behavior rather than the generic estimate. Older session anchors without a stored `scale` default to 1.0 to maintain backward compatibility.
ai.evidence: The diff adds an optional `scale` field to `contextTokenBaseline` in `common/src/types/session-state.ts` and updates `recordContextUsage` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/util/context-token-count.ts` to compute and clamp this ratio between `MIN_SCALE` (0.5) and `MAX_SCALE` (2.5).
ai.unknowns: The specific threshold or compaction trigger that benefits from the tighter estimate is not visible in this diff, only the mechanism that reduces estimation error.

changes.what: Adds optional `scale` field to the `contextTokenBaseline` type in `AgentState`.
Implements `MIN_SCALE`/`MAX_SCALE` bounds and applies the calibration factor in `estimateContextTokens`, `recordContextUsage`, and `adjustContextTokenCountForHistoryEdit`.
Passes the baseline `scale` into `adjustContextTokenCountForHistoryEdit` when building cancelled session states in `buildCancelledSessionState`.

eli5.text: The Freebuff team improved the system that tracks how much of the AI's memory window is filled during a coding session. Because different AI models count words and code differently, the previous estimate was sometimes too low, leading to miscalculations of how much room was left. This internal update allows the tool to measure its own counting accuracy against each model and adjust future calculations to stay well within safe limits. You will not see a new feature or need to change any settings; the assistant will simply manage its memory more reliably when handling long conversations.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.2.28 adds Anthropic version header to BYOK listing checks
ai.summary: The SDK now sends the required `anthropic-version` header when probing or discovering models for OpenAI-compatible BYOK connections pointing at `api.anthropic.com`, fixing a 400 error that occurred because Anthropic's native /models endpoint refuses requests lacking that header. The new `byokListingHeaders` function in `sdk/src/byok.ts` is consumed by `checkConnection` in `sdk/src/client.ts` and by the context-window discovery path in `byok.ts`, ensuring both validation and auto-sizing send the correct headers. This release packages several additional changes including the removal of Composio tools, a new desktop cloud agent module, and a per-model calibration scale for context token estimation.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.2.28 lets you run Claude Code and Codex directly inside cloud-based chats by saving your Anthropic or OpenAI API keys to your account. The release removes the built-in Composio tools for connecting external apps, replacing them with a new integration framework where you connect apps like Gmail or Slack through the settings menu. When you use your own API key for an Anthropic endpoint, the assistant now includes a required version header when checking which models are available, preventing connection errors. Context tracking is calibrated per-model so the assistant better estimates how much of your chat history is using up the available memory space. Additionally, the system now hashes email addresses before sending them to advertising partners for ad tracking, and custom domain setup for hosted sites now includes verification and status checks.

Nix's store holds the executables AND their dynamic loaders/libraries. A profile's bin directory alone is not a usable runtime. Only the store is exposed, read-only; /nix/var and the user's home remain outside the sandbox.

ai.title: SDK free mode suppresses BYOK keys and adds Nix-aware Linux sandboxing
ai.summary: The SDK model provider now honors a new `costMode` parameter in `getModelForRequest`, using `isFreeMode` to prevent inherited `BYOK_OPENROUTER` environment variables from being sent as headers in Freebuff's 'free' mode. A new module, `sdk/src/tools/sponsored-linux-runtime.ts`, replaces the previous hardcoded bubblewrap path lookup with a function that resolves Nix profile executables to their immutable `/nix/store` locations while ignoring project-local PATH entries. The Linux sponsored sandbox now mounts `SPONSORED_LINUX_RUNTIME_ROOTS` (including `/nix/store`) as read-only, rewrites the run's `PATH` and executable targets via `sponsoredLinuxSearchPath`, and replaces the `/bin/true` probe with a `/bin/sh -c 'exit 0'` check to support NixOS environments. This commit contains four distinct changes spanning provider credentialing and sandbox runtime resolution.
ai.evidence: In `sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts`, `getModelForRequest` now accepts a `costMode` parameter and calls `isFreeMode(costMode)` to suppress the `openrouterApiKey` resolution; in `sdk/src/tools/sponsored-sandbox.ts`, `findBubblewrap` is re-exported from the new `sdk/src/tools/sponsored-linux-runtime.ts` which adds Nix store path resolution via `sponsoredLinuxRuntimePath`.

ai.title: SDK BYOK OpenRouter 404 errors detect routing policy blocks
ai.summary: The SDK model provider now classifies specific OpenRouter 404 responses as routing-policy rejections rather than generic model-not-found errors. A new helper, isOpenRouterSettingsRejection, checks if the base URL belongs to an OpenRouter endpoint and if the error body matches phrases like "No allowed providers" or "No endpoints found matching your data policy". When detected, the error message changes to direct users to OpenRouter's privacy settings page to adjust their allowed providers or data retention policies, distinguishing configuration issues from actual missing models.
ai.evidence: The diff in sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts adds the private function isOpenRouterSettingsRejection which parses OpenRouter 404 response bodies for specific routing-policy messages, and updates getByokProviderErrorMessage to accept an openRouterSettingsRejected flag that triggers a dedicated diagnostic message directing users to OpenRouter's privacy settings page.

eli5.text: When you use your own AI provider key and the service refuses a request because of your privacy or provider settings, the assistant now explains exactly why it happened instead of showing a generic error. This affects people who bring their own external AI keys to connect to a specific routing service. You will see a clear message pointing you to the settings page so you can adjust your allowed providers or data policies, which prevents confusion from thinking the model itself was missing.
